reason: Charcoal and water may make ink for the printing press.
expectation: I expect a dark ink or pigment, though it may need another step.

alternatives.reason: Shaping planks could make part of the press, but I chose to prepare ink first.

effect: The ink is ready for the printing project, so I can work on its machinery.
reaction: That result matched my expectation; nothing notable.
reason: A chisel can shape planks into a component for the press.
expectation: I expect a shaped wooden part, though its exact purpose is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Stone and rope might make a clock weight, but I want to advance the press first.

effect: The shaped planks became a printing block, giving me a component for the press.
reaction: That makes sense as a surface for printing.
reason: Combining the block with iron seems like the next step toward building the press.
expectation: I expect iron to add a fitting or mechanism to the printing block, though the exact result is unclear.

alternatives.reason: Stone and rope may make a clock weight, but I want to continue the press first.

effect: The block and iron made a printing press, revealing the goal of printing a page.
reaction: The screw mechanism makes the combination clear and satisfying.
reason: The block needs ink to transfer an image onto paper.
expectation: I expect an inked press that can then print on paper.

alternatives.reason: Paper is also needed for the page, but inking the press first seems practical.

effect: The press is inked and ready for paper, as expected.
reaction: The explanation makes the next step clear.
reason: Adding paper should produce the page required by the goal.

effect: The printed pages complete the printing goal, leaving the clock to make.
reaction: The repeated illustration makes the purpose of the press clear.
reason: Stone and rope are the only offered combination, and they may make a weight for the clock.
expectation: I expect a suspended weight or pendulum component, though its exact role is uncertain.

effect: The stone and rope made a pendulum, providing a component for the clock.
reaction: That matches the suspected pendulum role.
reason: The pendulum and gear are the only offered combination and both fit the clock project.
expectation: I expect a clock or a clock mechanism connecting the pendulum to the gear.

effect: The pendulum and gear made clockwork, leaving a housing or support to complete the clock.
reaction: The result fits the clock project.
reason: Combining the clockwork with planks is the only offered action and may give it a case.
expectation: I expect a finished clock, perhaps with a wooden case.

effect: The planks housed the clockwork, completing the clock and the chapter.
reaction: The explanation of the pendulum and gears was satisfying, though the clock came together quickly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the printing press was most worthwhile: the description explained how the screw presses paper against the inked block.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final clock combinations felt brief and predictable, especially with only one action offered at each step.

surprise.text: The printing press description clarified how the carved block and iron formed a working screw press.

arbitrary.text: Making ink from charcoal and water was understandable as a dark pigment, though the process was simplified.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter if it offered more mechanisms to explore; the press was interesting, though the later single-option sequence gave me little to decide.
